newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Significant gain seen on Soundwill debut.
newsitem.headline: Significant gain seen on Soundwill debut.

text.p: Shares of property redevelopment concern Soundwill Holdings Ltd are poised for strong debut on Friday, extending the recent strong performance of new listings, analysts said.

"We expect the shares to debut strongly due to investors' recent strong interest in investing in new listings," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment. "The shares are likely to trade above its grey market price."
Brokers said the grey market price of the stock was at about HK$3.10 per share.
Soundwill engages in property investment and redevelopment in Hong Kong, in particular modern office towers and small to medium sized residential buildings.
Soundwill offered 300 million shares at HK$2.18 each in global offering, of which 15 percent of the issue offered to the public in Hong Kong had been 8.69 times oversubscribed.

Analysts said they expected the shares to have an upside of 20 to 50 percent, repeating the story of Kwong Hing International Holdings Ltd which its flotation was also about 8.35 times oversubscribed.
Shares of the knitted fabrics maker Kwong Hing which hit a day high of HK$1.56, closed at HK$1.45 on debut on Wednesday, up 20.83 percent from their issue price of HK$1.20.
However, there is concern that a possible oversupply of office property in Hong Kong in the long run can slow the company's earnings growth.
"We are a bit cautious on its future growth because we expect that there will be an oversupply of office property in coming years," said Pamela Lam, analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities.

"As the size of the company is relatively small (compared with other big developers), it is not easy for it to buy old buildings at a low cost (for redevelopment) and the process in redeveloping a site also involves quite a lot of time," another analyst said. "It will boost its cost in the long run."
Soundwill said the proceeds would be used to fund its purchase of property, for loan repayment and for working capital.
